text:
anya: quick update from this morning's hot-prune-v3 canary on helix. short summary first: tails down, token cost down, one shard hiccup. details below. :sparkles:

ops-bot: deploy: rollout hot-prune-v3 -> helix-canary-2 (12 hosts) at 2026-03-22T08:03:12Z

drew: high level numbers (canary vs baseline, matched traffic slice, 8hr run):
- p50 latency: 52ms -> 49ms (~6% improvement)
- p95 latency: 260ms -> 170ms (~35% improvement)
- p99 latency: 510ms -> 365ms (~28% improvement)
- estimated infra token cost per 1M tokens: $13.4 -> $12.3 (~8% savings)

maria: awesome. any regressions when requests have very low kv reuse?

anya: yes, small cold-path regressions for <2% kv-hit sequences. cold p5 went up by ~35ms in those slices. overall tail improved significantly though.

sam: can you share the prune parameters you ran? curious about thresholds and hold times.

anya: sure, canary config excerpt:

```
features.hot_prune:
  enabled: true
  mode: proactive
  utilization_target: 0.68
  scan_interval_ms: 2500
  min_live_ms: 20000
  max_batch_evict: 96
  protect_recent_prefix_ms: 12000
  shard_overrides: {}
```

drew: implementation details: v3 introduces a tiny MRU-protected warmset and sorts evict candidates by reuse score instead of LRU. that reduced churn under heavy concurrent writes and improved GPU kernel packing.

chris: checked error rates and SLOs during canary window 026-03-22 08:00-16:00 UTC. 5xx unchanged. we observed a 0.9% uptick in client-side circuit-breaker trips for one shard id=shd-09b. rolled that shard back to v2 at 2026-03-22T12:40Z.

anya: shd-09b had very bursty long-context flows that raced with background evictions and triggered higher latency spikes. proposed fix: shard-level min_live_ms override + a conservative mode for shards flagged as "burst_long_ctx". adding PR now.

sre_lead: please make sure rollback is simple. what's the exact flag to flip if we see more regressions on rollout?
drew: flip features.hot_prune.enabled=false via feature-control API, or set features.hot_prune.mode=passive to keep background decay only. both roll out in seconds. documented in the runtime playbook.

maria: can you paste the bench command used to simulate the regressed case? we'll add to oncall runbook.

anya: bench invocation we used to surface the issue:

```
bench-client --model redwood-13b --workers 48 --warmup 300 --requests 2500 --mix long_context:0.2,short:0.8 --kv_reuse_prob 0.03 --pin-shard shd-09b
```

chris: thanks. action items I want in the ticket:
1) add shard-level min_live_ms override and tag shards with "burst_long_ctx" if needed
2) run an extended canary (50 hosts) for 48h with seeded long-context traffic
3) update runbook with bench command, logs to collect, dashboard links, and rollback steps
4) monitor p99, cold p5, circuit-breaker hits, and evicted-entry churn rate

ops-bot: ticket created: RT-4602 026-hot-prune-v3-shard-overrides-and-extended-canary (assignee: anya)

anya: PR is up for the shard override logic: https://git.internal/r/pr/4532 (cc @sam @maria for review). adding conservative default for shards without override.

sam: tagging in review. we'll sanity-check defaults and make sure defaults don't punish low-reuse customers.

maria: please ensure metrics for "eviction_rate" and "protected_warmset_size" are in the dashboard so SRE can triage quickly.

anya: will add those metrics. preliminary note on why this improved tails: by evicting low-reuse prefix entries first and keeping a tiny MRU-protected warmset, we reduce large KV churn that used to block kernel scheduling. that made high-concurrency bursts schedule more compactly leading to lower p95/p99.

drew: TL;DR: solid tail wins and meaningful cost reduction, small cold-case regressions on very low-KV-reuse long-context bursts. mitigations ready (shard overrides) and we have quick rollback. recommended: schedule extended canary once PR and dashboards are in place.

sre_lead: approved for extended canary. please include dashboard links in the ticket and ping the oncall 30m prior to flip.

anya: thanks everyone 026-03-22. I'll post a short summary to #eng-runtime after extended canary finishes unless there are objections. :rocket:
